newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Fairfax sees economy affecting results.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Fairfax sees economy affecting results.

text.p: Newspaper publisher John Fairfax Ltd said on Wednesday the slower Australian economy coupled with higher newsprint prices will impact upon the group's final results for the year to June 30, 1997.

"Coupled with the state of the economy, Fairfax, in common with the whole newspaper industry, has had to face high newsprint prices and this, too, will impact upon our final results in the current year," Fairfax chairman Sir Laurence Street told the company's annual general meeting.
But Street said the company was optimistic about its long-term future.

"I shall not recapitulate the outline contained in the annual report that you have before you, but I believe it can be responsibly said that there is every reasion to be optimistic in forecasting the longer term future of our company," he told shareholders at the annual meeting.
Street said the group was in a strong position for the future after the new A$330 million printing plant at Chullora and the A$88 million upgrade of the printing plant in Melbourne.
Street said these investments were proving attractive to advertisers and there was some basis for sensing signs of a return to confidence in the marketplace.
"This will, in turn, be reflected in the company's revenue flow," he said.
Conrad Black's Hollinger International Inc owns 25 percent of Fairfax, while Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd holds 15 percent and Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd owns five percent.
Fairfax reported a 29.8 percent drop in 1995/96 (July-June) net profit before abnormals to A$101.5 million.
